Surface verdict: **not comparable**, one reason — `cache_read=11931993` and `cache_creation=242086` are both nonzero, so the $9.61 figure is a warm-cache cost and cannot be put beside cold runs. The retrieval metrics are unaffected. Everything else is clean: `commands.log` is present and my independent count matches the scorer's exactly (collateral_damage 23, stakeout 22, the_receipts 14, case_file 3, manhunt 2, roll_call/blueprint/rap_sheet/ToolSearch 1 each; 68 calls total). No filesystem or shell tool appears; every tool is inside the launcher's `--allowedTools` (including `rap_sheet`, which entered the list on 2026-09-17), and `ToolSearch` is the schema loader, not a checkout read. `stakeout` was exercised 22 times, so the retriever the arm is named for is the one measured. The fold probe reports all five of the arm's own top-5 seeded into `collateral_damage` across all seven lenses.

What the three misses share: they are the *consumer* server-side entry points for booking surfaces other than the two the run committed to. The arm locked onto the user/org and team **booking-page** axis — `[user]`, `[user]/[type]`, `org/[orgSlug]/…`, `team/[slug]/…` — and ranked that family densely and deeply, down to the embed and `queries.ts` variants. The three it never reached sit in adjacent booking surfaces that resolve the same branding through a different route: the routing-forms link page, the shared `lib/booking.ts` helper, and the booking-confirmation single view's own `getServerSideProps`. All three are `getServerSideProps`/lib-layer callers rather than view or repository code, and none of them carries the org/team-slug vocabulary the sweep was built around — `bookings-single-view.getServerSideProps.tsx` is the sharpest case, since its sibling `bookings-single-view.tsx` was ranked at 68 while the data-fetching half beside it was not.
